newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Stad R'dam sticks to div pay-out ratio.
newsitem.headline: Stad R'dam sticks to div pay-out ratio.

text.p: Dutch mid-sized insurer Stad Rotterdam clarified on Thursday that it would stick to its current dividend pay-out ratio of close to 50 percent.
On Wednesday chairman Carlo de Swart told Reuters the current dividend pay-out ratio was just over 48 percent.
"The dividend (pay-out) has to remain close to 50 percent," De Swart said on Thursday, exlaining that this did not imply an increase from the current level.
"Our pay-out ratio is two to three percent more than other financials," De Swart said.
Insurer Aegon had a pay-out ratio of 47 percent, ING 43 percent and Fortis Amev 44 percent.
Stad Rotterdam paid a dividend of 2.10 guilders per share in 1995, with earnings per share mounting to 4.39 guilders.
"We want to continue offering the option of taking the dividend either in cash or in share certificates," De Swart said, adding that in principle both would be roughly equal.
Fortis Amev and ING Groep each own 20 percent of Stad Rotterdam, while unlisted Achmea has five percent.
